title: Stress intensity factor solutions for weld root cracks in cruciform fillet-welded joints under combined bending and axial load

record.title: Stress intensity factor solutions for weld root cracks in cruciform fillet-welded joints under combined bending and axial load
record.abstract: Weld root cracks in cruciform fillet-welded joints are a common failure mode in steel bridge cross-girder connections yet SIF solutions for combined loading remain limited in the literature. This paper presents parametric finite element results for mode I stress intensity factors at weld root crack tips in cruciform joints with leg ratio a/T from 0.1 to 0.7 and plate thickness T from 12 to 40 mm, under 19 combinations of axial and in-plane bending loads. Three-dimensional models were built in Abaqus with refined meshes at the crack front using collapsed quadratic elements. Interaction integrals were used to extract KI values. The results were fitted to a polynomial correction function F(a/T, ρ, λ) with a maximum fitting error of 2.1% over the parametric space. Validation against three published experimental datasets showed mean deviation below 5%. The proposed solutions are intended for direct use in Paris-law integration routines for bridge connection fatigue assessment.
